<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba35dfd78283d5f839eaaaab24764322ae3e263a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ab082955615e4f4a65dd2287ecf7177aa88009ab`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.security-catalog-environment-overlay-refused.ts + none

Inputs read: card #33388 (body and comments 6882204943, 6884033142, 6884395326), PR #33445 (body, 4-file list, net diff against `main`), the check-runs on this head. No file in the diff implements or enforces the two `hits` files (the other two are a guide page and the changeset), so the `+` side is `none`; the enforcing code was read on `main`, not reviewed.

Check-runs on this head when read (2026-11-14): 24 success, 10 skipped, 31 still in progress, 0 failed. Concluded green include `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. Not concluded: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1..8/8)`, `Test UI (1..16/16)`, `Type Check · workspace / debt ledger / consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, three `Lint` families. This record judges the contract; it does not stand in for the runs that have not concluded, and the merge waits for them.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged. Right. The diff touches no Zod schema, no type union member and no constant: in `customization-package.ts` only two lines of the `OverrideClassificationBasis` doc comment move; `OverrideClassificationBasis`, `OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION` (`permission`, `position`, `capability` all `{ disposition: 'excluded', basis: 'adr_0146_d6_security_catalog' }`) are byte-identical.
- Public surface: one published string changes, the `reason` of the semantic migration entry `security-catalog-environment-overlay-refused` (ships in spec `dist/migrations` and in the generated upgrade guide). Right that it is published, right that it is prose only. `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `acceptanceCriteria` and the header comment are unchanged in the diff (the hunk is lines 27-29 of `reason` alone); from "A cold boot now refuses it too" to the end the `reason` is the same text.
- Migration matching: the entry's `id` is what a consumer keys on; it does not move, so nothing that selects or reports the entry changes.
- No generated artifact checked in carries the old sentence: on `main` it appears only at the edited line and in released CHANGELOG files (release-owned). `Spec property liveness` and `Type Check · source gates` are green.
- Guide page (`content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`): two sentences, both in the card's added scope (6882204943, N4 and N5). Judged in ④ because they state the same contract.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/33388-security-catalog-entry-reason.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch. Right: the only published change is the wording of one migration entry's `reason` plus a doc comment; no accept-set, type, id or behaviour moves, so neither minor nor major applies, and `skip-changeset` would be wrong because the string ships in `dist`. No other package publishes anything from this diff (the guide page belongs to no package). `Check Changeset` is green.

`Clause-②: no` on the PR body and in the changeset: right, nothing an author could write is newly accepted or refused. `Metadata-protocol: none`: right, no protocol surface, wire shape or door is touched. The title carries no `!`, and none is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6884395326 `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation 1 (PR body footer in the harness form): no contract effect; the seat's call.
- Deviation 2 (Human Minimum item 3 and "Before Submitting" unchecked, `pnpm lint` left to CI): `Lint · ESLint` and `Lint · docs & code guards` are green on this head; three other `Lint` families had not concluded when read.
- Out-of-scope finding, class a: `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` `coldBootConflictMessage` (:2818) and the hot-install text of `SecurityCatalogNameConflictError` (:2880) still say "Positions, permission sets and capabilities each hold one name per deployment: an assignment names a position or a permission set by its bare name". Confirmed on `main`. The refusals fire correctly; the stated reason is false for permission sets since a grant carries `permission_set_package`. Correctly left out of this card (runtime text of another package). ESCALATED to the seat: after this PR the migration entry and the runtime refusal it records give different reasons, so this needs its own card if it has none.
- Out-of-scope finding, no carrier (ADR-0048 addendum, ADR-0146 D6 text, test comments, released CHANGELOGs): accepted as left. Decision records and release-owned text are not this card's to rewrite. Note that ADR-0146 D6 itself still gives "They hold one name per deployment" as its reason; the gloss no longer repeats it, which is the card's TO.

### ④ Design judgment

**`18.security-catalog-environment-overlay-refused.ts`, `reason`.** New opening: "The environment catalog and a package never hold one name: a package registering a name the environment catalog already holds was already refused on a hot install."

- True at the hot-install door: `refuseSecurityCatalogNameConflicts` asks `securityCatalogHoldersOtherThan` with `environment: true`, and the ADR-0150 namespace narrowing in `add()` filters `kind === 'package'` holders only (`permissionSetHoldersMeet` "judges package holders alone: the environment's own set and a built-in name are refused by each door as before"). So an environment holder meets every package, permission sets included.
- True at the cold boot: `environmentHeldSecurityCatalogConflicts` reports every package-held position or permission-set name the bare slot also holds, with no namespace test, and the boot is refused.
- True at the save door: `permissionSetNameCollisionRefusal`, `meets()` returns true when either side is the environment (`holder === null || written === null`).
- Attempt to break it, built-in names: the item seam passes `environment: !BUILT_IN_SECURITY_CATALOG_NAMES[type].has(baseName)` and the cold boot skips built-in names, so an environment item can sit under a built-in name. That is the environment beside the PLATFORM's declaration, which the code classes `kind: 'built-in'`, not a package ("a built-in name is never available to a package"), and the entry's `surface` is rows under a name "a configured package declares". The sentence holds as written. The sentence it replaces had the same edge and was additionally false for permission sets.
- "was already refused on a hot install" and "A cold boot now refuses it too": the pronoun still resolves to "a package registering a name the environment catalog already holds". No drift against `surface` or `acceptanceCriteria` ("refused with NAMESPACE_CONFLICT (422) naming the environment catalog as the holder" matches `existingHolder: { kind: 'environment' }`).
- Matches the card's TO ("the environment catalog and a package never hold one name").
- F1, nit: the second fragment of the opening is one 165-character source line (line 28) where every neighbour wraps near 100. Source layout only; the concatenated string is correct (spacing checked) and `Lint · ESLint` is green. Fixing it would move the head; leave it.

**`customization-package.ts`, `adr_0146_d6_security_catalog` gloss.** "D6: the security catalog takes no override (permission sets, positions, capabilities)".

- Against the ADR: ADR-0146 D6 bullet "Permission sets, positions and capabilities are not overridable." The gloss now states the decision; it no longer states the ADR's own (now partly stale) reason. True.
- Against the constant it annotates: exactly the three rows `permission`, `position`, `capability` carry this basis, all `excluded`; `customization-package.test.ts:184` pins that. The parenthesis lists the same three.
- Against the first consumer: `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` maps the basis to the citation 'ADR-0146 D6' and refuses a declared override of an excluded type `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. "Takes no override" is what the gate does.
- Verbatim the card's TO. No finding.

**`permission-sets.mdx`** (not a `hits` file; read because it states the same contract).

- "a grant names its set by its package and name (`sys_user_permission_set.permission_set_package` and `permission_set`)": both columns exist and are what the resolver reads (`resolve-authz-context.ts` `GRANT_ROW_COLUMNS`; `stored-package-references.ts` R1). True, and now agrees with "each granted by its own package and name" below it.
- One-holder list gains "the environment": true at both doors (above), and the list is now the same members in the same order as the `PermissionSetSchema.name` describe on `main` ("two packages of one namespace, a package with no namespace, a platform package (base, system, sys), the environment and the platform-requested guest_portal"), which is `permissionSetHoldersMeet` plus the environment. No finding.

Findings: F1 nit. No must-fix, no should-fix. The round ends on nits.
